newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Commission President Jacques Santer had met former Commission President Jacques Delors on Friday morning to discuss changes to the way the Commission works in the framework of the inter-governmental conference (IGC). Van der Pas said Santer would invite other former Commission presidents to discuss the same issue.
Spokesmen Joao Vale de Almeida, Peter Guilford, Nicolaas Wegter and Josep Coll i Carbo briefed on Monday and Tuesday's General Affairs Council.

Vale de Almeida said main points in Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro's field would be the EU-South Africa negotiations, the overseas territories and countries and the situation in the Great Lakes and Zaire. He said the nomination of the European Electoral Unit President should be confirmed at the Council.
Guilford said trade discussions would focus on leghold traps, the Geneva telecoms agreement, relations with China, including the human rights aspects, and the Helms-Burton dispute.
Wegter said Balkans issues would be the emergency programme for most needy people in Bulgaria, the state of play in EU-Albanian relations and the situation in ex-Yougoslavia.

He also said the ministers would prepare the association council with Cyprus on Tuesday afternoon at 1400/1300 GMT. Wegter said Commissioner Hans van den Broek and the EU representative for Cyprus would visit Cyprus from Wednesday to Friday to discuss future negotiations with Cyprus, to start six months after the end of the IGC, and the international efforts to find a solution to the Cyprus issue.

Coll i Carbo said Commission President Jacques Santer, Commissioner Manuel Marin and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat would meet on Monday around 1500/1400 GMT in the Council building. He said they would also sign the EU-Palestinian Authority interim association accord at 1830/1730 GMT, followed by a news conference.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/139: Making Europe accessible for tourists with disabilities - A handbook for the tourism industry.
- IP/97/140: Proposal for a directive to reduce emissions from light commercial vehicles.
- IP/97/144: Commission clears acquisition by Archer-Daniels-Midland company of Grace Cocoa Associates.
- IP/97/145: Commission approves joint venture between Telia and Ericsson.
- IP/97/146: The Commission approves merger in the temporary employment services sector.
- IP/97/147: The Commission adopts a statement of objections against Unilever concerning freezer cabinet exclusivity in the Irish ice cream market.
- Memo/97/18: Calendar of the Commission's activities for February 23-28, 1997.
- Eurostat news release No 16/97: Eurostat takes further decisions on deficit and debt.
- Eurostat news release No 17/97: EU industrial production up by only 0.3% last year.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and finance No 1997-5: Food price levels in Europe.
